rules: Current INSPIRE download index states the dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
The dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly publication represents data from the previous month.
INSPIRE polygons are separated into files for each local authority.
London Borough of Haringey is listed in the current download index.
The files are published in GML format.
A GIS is required to view and work with the downloaded polygons.
INSPIRE is a subset covering registered freehold land and property.
The public INSPIRE dataset covers England and Wales.
Polygons show indicative position and extent, not definitive legal extent.
The individual title plan is required to identify the registered extent.
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID.
The INSPIRE ID relates the polygon to a registered title.
A single title can contain several separate polygons.
Each polygon in a multi-polygon title has its own INSPIRE ID.
Land without an INSPIRE ID may be unregistered.
Land without an INSPIRE ID may be leasehold or another excluded tenure.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are available for reuse under the OGL.
Polygon coordinates are captured against the British National Grid.
Reprojection from BNG to WGS84 may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The current Haringey GML link still enters a redirect loop in this execution environment.
Exact current Haringey GML bytes and SHA-256 were not captured.
Candidate containment cannot be tested without exact current polygon bytes.
No exact current INSPIRE ID and title-plan binding was read back.

Planning Data entity pages support HTML representations.

Bulk dataset downloads are available as JSON.

The direction dataset is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
The dataset states some records originate from MHCLG and are being replaced by authoritative sources.
Article 4 area geometry is represented as polygon or multipolygon.
Area references are intended to be unique and permanent.
Each area links to its Article 4 direction reference.

The 1m DTM is published by the Environment Agency.
The composite DTM covers approximately 99% of England.
The composite DTM has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse return.
Surface objects are removed using algorithms and manual editing.
The resulting product represents the terrain surface.
The current composite was produced in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where surveys repeat, the newest best-resolution data is used.
Bilinear interpolation is used where data is resampled.
Composite input surveys span 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Data is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 km tiles.
Heights are in metres, referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Input surveys have vertical accuracy of ±15 cm RMSE.
The dataset coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The dataset is published under the Open Government Licence.
The dataset metadata states an annual update frequency.
A WCS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
A WMS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
A WMTS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
An OGC API Features service is listed.

The OS Data Hub page reports the current OS Terrain 50 version date as July 2026.
OS Terrain 50 is freely downloadable OpenData under the OGL.
The product covers all of Great Britain.
The product models ground surface after protruding features are removed.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use 10 km by 10 km National Grid tiles.
The grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
Standard contour polylines use a 10 metre interval.
The grid is supplied as ASCII Grid and GML.
Contours are supplied as Shapefile, GML, GeoPackage and vector tiles.
The standard tile header specifies 200 rows.
The standard tile header specifies a 50 metre cell size.
Grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
Tiles are arranged into 55 folders representing 100 km grid squares.
The full national grid supply is documented as 157 MB compressed.
GeoPackage is supplied as one national flat file.
Vector tiles are supplied as one national MBTiles file.
OS OpenData download operations do not require an API key.
The Downloads API accepts TQ as an area filter and returns 307 when redirect selects exactly one file.
